overview: This Senate resolution honors the life of Mia Love, a former U.S. Representative from Utah who died on March 23, 2025. It notes that she was born in Brooklyn to Haitian immigrant parents, became the first African-American woman elected mayor in Utah, and in 2014 became the first Black Republican woman elected to Congress. It describes her later work as a commentator and author and her memoir recorded after her cancer diagnosis. The resolution expresses the Senate's sorrow, sends a copy to her family, and adjourns the Senate in her memory. The Senate agreed to it on April 5, 2025.
for: Supporters say it rightly honors a trailblazing public servant whose story inspired many people, especially women and children of immigrants.
against: Critics say it is a symbolic gesture that does not change any law or spending.
